title: Expert Witness Report Excerpt - Toxic Tort Litigation
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

HOUSTON DIVISION

LINDA O’NEIL-MENDOZA,    )
                  Plaintiff,    )
                               )
v.                            )   Civil Action No. 4:25-cv-01197
                               )
CHEMTECH SOLUTIONS, INC.,     )
                  Defendant.   )

EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF DR. ANTHONY P. GRANT, P.E., C.S.P.

I, Dr. Anthony P. Grant, P.E., C.S.P., Bar Number 24098765, do hereby submit this report pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(a)(2). My curriculum vitae is attached as Exhibit A. My billing rate is $550 per hour. All opinions expressed herein are based upon my education, training, and experience in the field of industrial hygiene and chemical exposure assessment.

1. Assignment
I was retained by counsel for Plaintiff, Deborah Bryant of Bryant Law Firm, P.C., to evaluate whether Defendant ChemTech Solutions, Inc. failed to implement adequate safety protocols at its facility located at 4500 Industrial Parkway, Pasadena, Texas 77507, resulting in the toxic exposure of Plaintiff Linda O’Neil-Mendoza.

2. Background Facts
Plaintiff Linda O’Neil-Mendoza was employed as a chemical operator at the ChemTech plant from January 2018 until her termination in October 2022. On or about March 12, 2022, she was exposed to a cloud of methylene chloride vapors after a valve malfunction. Her date of birth is July 15, 1985. She subsequently developed chronic respiratory conditions. I reviewed her medical records, which include notes from Dr. Sarah K. Lin, M.D., of Memorial Hermann Hospital. I also reviewed internal company emails, including one from plant manager John R. Thomas to the safety director with subject line "Ventilation issues." The email address of Plaintiff’s counsel is dbryant@bryantlawfirm.com. I also reviewed a telephone log containing a call from Plaintiff to her attorney at 713-555-0192.

3. Documents Reviewed
I have examined the following documents: (a) Plaintiff’s employment file (Bates range CHEMTECH0001-0350); (b) Material Safety Data Sheets for methylene chloride; (c) expert report of defense expert Dr. Harold F. Mercer; (d) deposition transcript of exhibitJohn Doe, a former ChemTech shift supervisor; (e) ChemTech’s internal safety audit from February 2022; (f) Plaintiff’s Social Security number, which appears in her personnel file as 456-78-9012; and (g) Defendant’s insurance policy number PLX-882-4410-00.

4. Summary of Opinions
It is my opinion, to a reasonable degree of engineering and scientific certainty, that ChemTech Solutions, Inc. violated industry standards for ventilation and personal protective equipment. The relevant standard is found in 29 C.F.R. § 1910.1052, which governs occupational exposure to methylene chloride. ChemTech’s own records show that air monitoring was not performed weekly as required. The permissible exposure limit was exceeded on at least three occasions in March 2022. This is consistent with precedents such as Smith v. ChemCo, 982 F.3d 410 (5th Cir. 2021), and Martinez v. Industrial Supply Co., 855 F. Supp. 2d 687 (S.D. Tex. 2018). In Smith, the court noted that “the failure to conduct adequate air monitoring constitutes gross negligence.” The Honorable Judge Richard A. Castillo presided over the Martinez case. In her deposition, Plaintiff testified that “[O’Neil-Mendoza] was told the valves were safe.”

5. Vehicle Incident
The day after her exposure, Plaintiff drove her 2019 Ford Explorer (VIN 1FM5K8GC2KKA12345) to the emergency room. The vehicle’s log shows she arrived at 2:15 P.M.

6. Conclusion
Defendant’s actions were a proximate cause of Plaintiff’s injuries. I reserve the right to supplement this report.

Dated: April 10, 2025

/s/ Dr. Anthony P. Grant, P.E., C.S.P.

Attest: Deborah Bryant, Attorney at Law

title: Expert Witness Report Excerpt - Medical Malpractice
text:
CAUSE NO. 2025-03678

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS
269TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

MAYA R. JENKINS,               )
                  Plaintiff,    )
                               )
v.                            )
                               )
DR. KEVIN J. THORNE, M.D.,    )
                  Defendant.   )

EXPERT REPORT OF DR. LAURA H. GOMEZ, M.D., F.A.C.S.

I, Dr. Laura H. Gomez, M.D., F.A.C.S., Bar Number 87654321, am a board-certified surgeon. I was retained by counsel for Plaintiff, Mark O’Malley of O’Malley & Associates, P.L.L.C. I submit this report per Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 74.351.

1. Background
Plaintiff Maya R. Jenkins, date of birth August 4, 1990, underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed by Defendant Dr. Kevin J. Thorne on March 15, 2024, at Gulf Coast Surgical Center (an organization). During the procedure, a bile duct injury occurred. The plaintiff’s postoperative course was complicated by sepsis. I reviewed the medical records with Bates range GCSC-0001-0420. The plaintiff’s insurance policy number is MHP-993-2258-66. Her phone number is 832-555-0147. Her counsel’s email is momalley@omalleyassociates.com. The defendant’s medical license number is L-4567. The plaintiff’s Social Security number is 234-56-7890.

2. Standard of Care
The standard of care for laparoscopic cholecystectomy requires proper identification of the cystic duct and artery before clipping. I cite as support the opinion in Henderson v. Surgical Partners, 640 S.W.3d 501 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2021). The court in that case noted, “[Thorne] failed to follow the critical view of safety.” The editorial brackets around “[Thorne]” replace the actual defendant’s name in the original opinion. Another relevant case is Davis v. Memorial Health, 501 F. Supp. 3d 556 (S.D. Tex. 2020).

3. Vehicle and Contact
The defendant’s vehicle, a 2021 Lexus RX 350 (VIN 2T2HZMAA1LC123456), was observed in the hospital parking lot on the day of surgery. The court is presided over by the Honorable Judge Patricia A. Nguyen.

4. Opinion
To a reasonable medical probability, Dr. Kevin J. Thorne deviated from the standard of care. The statutory requirement under Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 74.351(r)(6) is satisfied by this report.

Dated: May 1, 2025

/s/ Dr. Laura H. Gomez, M.D., F.A.C.S.

IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE WESTERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS

JAMES T. CARTER,               )
                  Plaintiff,    )
                               )
v.                            )   Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-00345
                               )
AUSTIN HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS,     )
                  Defendant.   )

EXPERT REPORT OF DR. ELENA M. VASQUEZ, PH.D.

I, Dr. Elena M. Vasquez, Ph.D., Bar Number 11223344, am a forensic economist. I was retained by counsel for Defendant, Sarah K. Langley of Langley & Hart, P.C. I submit this report to analyze economic damages.

1. Plaintiff’s Employment
Plaintiff James T. Carter, date of birth November 5, 1978, was employed as a registered nurse at Austin Healthcare Systems from 2015 until his termination on August 1, 2024. He claims discrimination based on age. The defendant’s human resources director is Paul R. Winters. The plaintiff’s Social Security number is 345-67-8901. His phone number is 512-555-0321. His email is james.carter1978@email.com. The defendant’s policy number is EMP-445-6677-89. The case was assigned to the Honorable Judge Michael T. Chang.

2. Methodology
I calculated lost wages using a discount rate of 3%. I reviewed the personnel file (Bates range AHS-100-250). I also reviewed the deposition of exhibitPaul R. Winters, where he testified about performance reviews. I considered the legal standard under 42 U.S.C. § 2000e-2. Relevant case law includes Taylor v. City of Dallas, 958 F.3d 366 (5th Cir. 2020), and Bryant v. TechCorp, 487 F. Supp. 3d 512 (W.D. Tex. 2019). In Bryant, the court stated, “[Carter] failed to show pretext.” The vehicle the plaintiff drove to his deposition was a 2020 Honda Accord (VIN 1HGCV1F37LA012345).

3. Conclusion
Plaintiff’s lost wages total $247,000 as of the date of this report.

Dated: June 15, 2025

/s/ Dr. Elena M. Vasquez, Ph.D.

CAUSE NO. DC-25-08941

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS
116TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

ROBERTA J. WHITFIELD,         )
                  Plaintiff,    )
                               )
v.                            )
                               )
ALLIED MANUFACTURING CO.,      )
                  Defendant.   )

EXPERT REPORT OF MR. THOMAS R. HENDRICKS, P.E.

I, Thomas R. Hendricks, P.E., Bar Number 99887766, am a mechanical engineer. I was retained by counsel for Plaintiff, Amanda L. Foster of Foster & Gonzalez, LLP. I submit this report regarding a defective lawnmower.

1. Incident
On June 10, 2023, Plaintiff Roberta J. Whitfield, date of birth April 30, 1982, sustained a severe laceration when the blade of a Model X-2000 lawnmower manufactured by Allied Manufacturing Co. detached. The mower’s serial number is VIN 4U7AA12345. The plaintiff’s Social Security number is 567-89-0123. Her phone is 214-555-0087. Her email is rwhitfield@myemail.com. Her homeowner’s insurance policy number is HO-334-2290-12. The defendant’s corporate counsel is James R. O’Neil of O’Neil Law Group. The court is presided over by the Honorable Judge Kevin D. Parker.

2. Defect Analysis
I examined the mower (Bates range ALLIED-EXH-001-150). The blade retention bolt was made of substandard steel. This violates the requirements of Tex. Prop. Code § 82.001. Relevant cases include Walker v. ToolCorp, 789 F.3d 654 (5th Cir. 2015), and Nelson v. GreenMower, 620 S.W.3d 444 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2020). In Nelson, the court noted, “[Whitfield] had no warning of the defect.”

3. Damages
Medical expenses total $128,000. Lost wages are estimated at $45,000.

Dated: July 20, 2025

/s/ Thomas R. Hendricks, P.E.

                               )
INNOVATIVE PACKAGING GROUP,    )

EXPERT REPORT OF DR. ROBERT C. MARTINEZ, PH.D., C.P.A.

I, Dr. Robert C. Martinez, Ph.D., C.P.A., Bar Number 55443322, am a forensic accountant. I was retained by counsel for Plaintiff, Janet O’Reilly of O’Reilly & Sons, P.C. I submit this report to quantify damages from a breach of a supply agreement.

1. Contract Terms
Global Logistics Solutions and Innovative Packaging Group entered into a contract on January 15, 2024. The defendant failed to deliver 10,000 custom pallets by the agreed date. The plaintiff’s CEO is William T. Grant. The defendant’s operations manager is Susan A. Chen. The plaintiff’s principal place of business is 1200 Commerce Street, Fort Worth, Texas 76102. The defendant’s policy number is COM-776-5432-11. The plaintiff’s Social Security number (for its guarantor, William T. Grant) is 678-90-1234. Phone: 817-555-0469. Email: info@globallogistics.com. The case was assigned to the Honorable Judge Robert L. Harrison.

2. Analysis
I reviewed the purchase orders (Bates range GLS-001-500). I also reviewed the deposition of exhibitSusan A. Chen. The applicable statute is Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 2.713. Relevant case law includes Evans v. SupplyChain, 913 F.3d 477 (5th Cir. 2019), and Thomas v. PalletCo, 734 S.W.3d 312 (Tex. App.—Fort Worth 2022). In Thomas, the court stated, “[Grant] was entitled to cover damages.” The vehicle used by the plaintiff’s logistics manager is a 2022 Ford F-150 (VIN 1FTFW1E84NFA67890).

3. Conclusion
Damages total $1,350,000.

Dated: August 10, 2025

/s/ Dr. Robert C. Martinez, Ph.D., C.P.A.
